en.body:
Few names in jazz command immediate recognition like Miles Davis or John Coltrane, but the ripples of talent and innovation spread much further. One such vital, though perhaps less celebrated, figure is the late trumpet virtuoso **Marcus Belgrave**. His profound impact on the landscape of American music is now the subject of the compelling documentary "...And Damn He Could Play: The Marcus Belgrave Story," directed by **Timashion Jones**.

The film aims to bring Belgrave's significant contributions out of the shadows and into the spotlight he so richly deserved. Born in Chester, Pennsylvania, and finding his artistic home in Detroit, Belgrave's career began remarkably early, making his professional debut at just 12 years old. His journey saw him collaborating with titans like **Ray Charles**, **Charles Mingus**, and, crucially, becoming an integral part of **Motown's Funk Brothers**, the uncredited session band behind countless hits. Mentored by the legendary **Clifford Brown**, Belgrave himself became a pivotal educator and mentor, shaping the careers of numerous musicians and nurturing Detroit's vibrant artistic community through his involvement with the groundbreaking **Tribe** arts collective.

## A Symphony of Voices for a Detroit Giant

The documentary boasts an impressive roster of artists who speak to Belgrave's enduring influence. The trailer alone features insights from jazz luminaries such as **Wynton Marsalis**, **Terence Blanchard**, **Regina Carter**, and **James Carter**, alongside figures like **Don Was** and **Ray Parker Jr.** This constellation of talent underscores the breadth of Belgrave's reach, not only as a performer but as a guiding force for generations. His mentorship is evident in the artistry of musicians like **Geri Allen**, **Kenny Garrett**, **Theo Croker**, and **Endea Owens**, many of whom are expected to be featured in the film. The narrative, brought to life by the distinctive voice of actor **Wendell Pierce**, promises to be an intimate portrait of a musician whose sound and spirit continue to inspire.

## Why Belgrave's Story Resonates

For fans of jazz, funk, soul, and the rich tapestry of American music, this documentary is a must-see. It shines a much-needed light on an artist whose influence is woven into the fabric of music history, yet whose name may not be as widely known as his contemporaries. Belgrave's dedication to his craft, his commitment to education, and his role in fostering a thriving arts scene in Detroit make his story a powerful testament to artistic passion and community building. "...And Damn He Could Play" is more than just a biographical film; it's a celebration of a legacy that continues to echo through the music we love, reminding us of the vital importance of recognizing and honoring all the architects of our cultural soundscape.

## What's Next

"...And Damn He Could Play: The Marcus Belgrave Story" is set to have its world premiere at **DOC NYC** on November 13. Following its premiere, audiences can anticipate further screenings and potential wider distribution, bringing this essential story to jazz enthusiasts and music lovers worldwide.

content_raw: He may not be a household name when it comes to the world of jazz, but the influence of Marcus Belgrave is felt far and wide, playing with Ray Charles, Charles Mingus, the Funk Brothers, and more. His life story now gets the documentary treatment with …And Damn He Could Play: The Marcus Belgrave Story , directed by Timashion Jones and featuring narration from Wendell Pierce. Ahead of its DOC NYC world premiere on November 13, we’re pleased to exclusively debut the first trailer and poster. The documentary features quite the lineup of appearances, including Wynton Marsalis, Don Was, Terence Blanchard, Bert Daring, Bill Meyer, Carl Craig, Charlie Gabriel, Chris Collins, Christopher Smith, Daphne Nitiri, David Ritz, Duke Fakir, Dwight Adams, Endea Owens, Eudora Muhammad, Gayelynn McKinney, Herb Boyd, James Carter, Joan Belgrave, Kasan Belgrave, Karriem Riggins, Mable John, Marion Hayden, Nicholas Peyton, Paul Riser, Ray Parker Jr., Regina Carter, Robert Hurst, Sheila Jordan, Theo Croker, Tonya Hood, and Wendell Harrison. Here’s the synopsis: “A jazz legend you likely haven’t heard of, trumpet player Marcus Belgrave’s influence has reverberated far beyond the spotlight. Making his professional debut at the age of 12, Belgrave went on to perform and record with the likes of Ray Charles, Charles Mingus, and Motown’s legendary Funk Brothers. Mentored by trumpet icon Clifford Brown, Belgrave in turn became a guiding force for generations of musicians through his work as an educator and mentor, championing Detroit’s artistic soul, and involvement in the groundbreaking arts collective Tribe. His reach can be heard in the artistry of jazz luminaries including Geri Allen, Kenny Garrett, James Carter, Regina Carter, Theo Croker, and Endea Owens, among many others. Though too often overlooked in the broader story of jazz, Belgrave’s legacy lives on in the musicians he inspired, the Detroit scene he helped cultivate, and the music that continues to swing, soar, and speak through generations.” “As a filmmaker from Detroit, I have always been drawn to stories that show the power of reaching and teaching the next generation. The children are our future, and it is only right that we pour into them and pass the baton so they can run and lead us forward. That is exactly what Marcus did through his music and mentorship,” said director Timashion Jones. “This documentary is my way of honoring that spirit and showing the world how one man could be a shattered diamond who shared his light and love for music with people all across the world. His story reminds us that when you invest in others, your legacy continues to play long after your final note.” See the exclusive trailer and poster premiere below.
